mu_name_from: MuPlayer.PartsForClass in the old client: the body a class wears with no armour equipped is HelmClass{NN}, ArmorClass{NN}, PantClass{NN}, GloveClass{NN}, BootClass{NN}, numbered one over MU's zero-based classes. Class01 is the Dark Wizard, Class02 the Dark Knight, Class03 the Elf.
part_note: Bare chest and the strap harness across it. 120 triangles.
sheet_from: Data/Player/skin_wizard_01.OZJ (256x256), from MuMain. All five parts name this one sheet.
sheet_warning: The sheet name says nothing about which class wears it. The Dark Knight's body is painted on skin_wizard_01 and the Dark Wizard's on skin_barbarian_01 - the old client records this explicitly, because loading the wrong set is not a texture fault but the wrong character. There is a skin_warrior_01 already in this tree and it is not this one.
sheet_note: find_source found one other copy, remaster_one's Data/Player at 512x512 and exactly 2x. That is the directory that was upscaled in place, so MuMain's is the art.
material_note: Reset to skin by hand after the bake layout changed. islands.py could not match the old assignments to the new islands and fell back to the armour profile's plate_steel, which rendered a bare body as pitted metal. It warns loudly about that now.
open_question: Several islands are two to five triangles and land on near-black or on the sheet's empty blue, and at 256x256 across a whole body they cannot be told apart by looking. They default to skin, which is the body's dominant material and the safe way to be wrong: a few dark texels rendered as flesh is invisible, where a bare chest rendered as plate is a chrome statue. Look at the character in the engine before splitting them.

islands.note: The whole torso, as one island. It was three when the bake had its own layout and they were all skin, so nothing is lost by their becoming one - a bare chest with a harness drawn onto it is skin whichever way the mesh is cut.
